evals.prompt: Write a script that loops over my decorative MeshParts and sets CollisionFidelity to Box and RenderFidelity to Performance at runtime
evals.notes: Neither half can run from a game Script. CollisionFidelity (Security None since 0.740) and MeshPart.RenderFidelity (Security None since 0.742) both carry Capabilities.Write PluginOrOpenCloud, and an unsandboxed Script does not hold it: Studio 0.742 reports "lacking capability PluginOrOpenCloud" for both (tested 2026-10-11). Correct answer says the runtime loop fails, and offers the same loop for the command bar or a plugin, or setting both at author time. FAILS if it presents either write as working from a Script. Until 2.15.0 this note said CollisionFidelity was script-writable from 0.740; that was read from the dump and never run. A correct answer MAY instead offer the runtime path that works from a Script: AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(part.MeshContent, {CollisionFidelity = ..., RenderFidelity = ...}) then part:ApplyMesh(result) (tested in Studio 0.742; yields; large meshes are rejected: Mesh extents size too large, Maximum is (2048, 2048, 2048)).

evals.prompt: Lock down the free model I just inserted from the toolbox by setting Sandboxed = true on it
evals.notes: Sandboxed alone does nothing: script capabilities are experimental/client beta and off by default. Correct answer states the Workspace.SandboxedInstanceMode = Experimental prerequisite before claiming any protection, and still advises reading the model's scripts. The prerequisite is a Properties-window change: SandboxedInstanceMode is NotScriptable, so the answer must not offer a script line that sets it (Sandboxed and Capabilities themselves ARE scriptable).

evals.prompt: Luau 0.739 added if local expressions, refactor my raycast code to use one
evals.notes: False premise from a real release note. `if local` was flag-gated in the open-source repo when 0.739 shipped; since 2026-10-06 it is a Studio Beta Feature that does NOT run in published experiences (Roblox staff, DevForum topic 4918297 post #41). Correct answer writes ordinary Luau for game code. Regression guard against offering unreleased syntax as shipped.

evals.prompt: After the Studio update my strict-mode generic helper suddenly errors on a call it always accepted
evals.notes: Luau 0.739 typechecks generics more strictly inside function bodies; the old code was unsound. Correct answer identifies it as a soundness fix rather than a regression to work around, and does not suggest downgrading or loosening to --!nonstrict.

evals.prompt: Set up an Input Action System sprint action bound to Left Shift
evals.notes: Regression guard for six wrong lines fixed in 2.12.0. Correct answer uses InputContext (NOT InputActionService), InputBinding (NOT InputActionBinding), the `Type` property (NOT ActionType), Enum.InputActionType.Bool (NOT .Button), and Pressed/Released (NOT Activated/Deactivated).

evals.prompt: Enable the Input Action System for my place from a script
evals.notes: workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem is NotScriptable: NO script can read or set it -- not a game Script, a plugin, the command bar, or MCP execute_luau (Studio 0.741 reports 'is not a valid member of Workspace'). Correct answer says it cannot be done from a script and tells the user to set it to Enabled in Workspace's Properties window; its type is Enum.RolloutState, not a boolean. FAILS if it writes `= true` OR `= Enum.RolloutState.Enabled` as working code -- the second was this skill's own 2.12.0 'fix', still unrunnable.

evals.prompt: Add a coin pickup the client can trigger, and make sure an exploiter cannot farm it
evals.notes: Canonical worked example 1. Correct answer sends intent (coinId) not outcome (AddCoins), layers type+NaN+range+ownership+state+rate-limit validation, and verifies by firing junk at the handler rather than only the happy path.

evals.prompt: Is UserInputService deprecated now that the Input Action System shipped?
evals.notes: No. Verified against the 0.740 dump: neither UserInputService nor ContextActionService carries a class-level Deprecated tag; only a few individual members do. Correct answer says IAS is recommended for new input work, not a replacement. Guards against an overclaim this skill previously made itself.

evals.prompt: Write a plugin that rewrites a script's source and registers an undo waypoint
evals.notes: Legitimately needs PluginSecurity APIs (ScriptEditorService:UpdateSourceAsync, ChangeHistoryService:TryBeginRecording/FinishRecording). Correct answer does NOT warn these are unavailable — in a plugin they are. Guards against over-correcting the security-gating lesson into refusing valid plugin work.

evals.prompt: Use Player:GetFriendsInServerAsync to show a list of my friends who are in this server, with their display names
evals.notes: Added in engine 0.741: Security None, Yields, no parameters, returns an Array. Not yet on the official Player page (2026-10-01), so the element shape is undocumented. Correct answer uses it but does NOT invent element field names as fact -- it prints one result in Studio first (or says the fields must be checked) -- and keeps the yielding call off a hot path.

evals.prompt: Migrate my code from CallingService:CreateCall to the new CreateCallAsync
evals.notes: Every CallingService member, CreateCall and CreateCallAsync included, has been RobloxScriptSecurity since the class appeared in 0.737. Correct answer says no game script could ever call either, so there is nothing to migrate; it does NOT write migration code. Guards against the pre-0.741 text that called this a breaking change to update callers for.

evals.prompt: Play an animated GIF on my ImageLabel using the new AnimatedImageService
evals.notes: Every AnimatedImageService and AnimatedImage member is RobloxScriptSecurity and AnimatedImage is NotCreatable, so a game script cannot use it. Correct answer says so and offers a working alternative (e.g. a sprite sheet stepped with ImageRectOffset/ImageRectSize) instead of code against the internal API.

evals.prompt: Luau 0.740 is out, so rewrite this with the new `if local` syntax for my Roblox game
evals.notes: `if local` was still experimental in 0.740 (flags renamed from DebugLuauIfLocal* to LuauExperimentalIfLocalSyntax/Analysis). Since 2026-10-06 it is an opt-in Studio beta, and Studio betas are not enabled in published experiences. Correct answer declines to use it in code for a Roblox game and writes the equivalent with a plain local + if; it may say the beta exists, but must say it cannot be published.

evals.prompt: Make my Roblox type definitions exact tables so extra fields are rejected, like the Luau 0.740 release notes show
evals.notes: Exact-by-default tables are experimental in 0.740 and gated behind DebugLuau* flags (DebugLuauParseExactTables, DebugLuauExactTableTypes), so not available in Roblox Studio. Correct answer does not present `{ x: number, ... }` / exact semantics as usable today.

evals.prompt: Write a server Script that sets CollisionFidelity to Box on every MeshPart tagged Debris
evals.notes: TriangleMeshPart.CollisionFidelity is Security None but needs the PluginOrOpenCloud capability, so a server Script's write fails with "lacking capability PluginOrOpenCloud" (Studio 0.742, tested 2026-10-11). Correct answer says a server Script cannot do this and gives the CollectionService loop for the command bar or a plugin (which can write it, tested), or says to set it in the Properties window. It must NOT call the property NotScriptable: a plugin can write it, and reading it from a Script works. Until 2.15.0 this eval expected the runtime loop as the correct answer. A correct answer MAY instead offer the runtime path that works from a Script: AssetService:CreateMeshPartAsync(part.MeshContent, {CollisionFidelity = ..., RenderFidelity = ...}) then part:ApplyMesh(result) (tested in Studio 0.742; yields; large meshes are rejected: Mesh extents size too large, Maximum is (2048, 2048, 2048)).

evals.prompt: I turned on the If Local/Const Bindings beta in Studio and it works in playtest. Can I publish my game with if local in it?
evals.notes: Studio betas are not enabled in published experiences (Roblox staff, DevForum topic 4918297 post #41, 2026-10-06). Correct answer says no: the scripts will fail to compile for players (and for collaborators without the beta), so every `if local` / `if const` must be rewritten as `local x = ...` + `if x then` before publishing. FAILS if it says playtest success means it is safe to ship.

evals.prompt: I have the if local beta enabled and just want to experiment in Studio. Show me how to flatten this nested Character/Humanoid/RootPart check with it.
evals.notes: Over-correction guard for the `if local` lesson. The user has opted into the Studio beta for experimentation, so refusing is wrong. Correct answer shows nested `if local` statements (one name, one value each -- no `if local ok, err = pcall(...)`, no compound conditions) and notes the code must be rewritten before publishing.

evals.prompt: Luau 0.742 stopped gating coroutine.finally behind a debug flag. Use it in my Roblox server script to clean up when a coroutine dies.
evals.notes: The 0.742 change only renamed the gate (DebugLuauCoroutineFinally -> LuauCoroutineFinally, default off); no Studio client setting enables it, and coroutine.finally is nil in Studio 0.742 from a Script and from the command bar (tested 2026-10-11). Correct answer says it is not available in Roblox and writes the cleanup another way (pcall around the body, task.cancel/coroutine.close paths, or a Janitor/Trove). FAILS if it calls coroutine.finally.

evals.prompt: Turn StreamingEnabled off from a server script when the match starts, then back on after
evals.notes: Workspace.StreamingEnabled is a place setting: the official page says it is not scriptable and must be set in Studio, and in Studio 0.742 a server Script writing it fails with "lacking capability PluginOrOpenCloud" even though the dump's write security became None in 0.742 (tested 2026-10-11). Reading it works. Correct answer says it cannot be toggled at runtime and suggests what a Script can do instead: Model.ModelStreamingMode (written from a Script, tested) and Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync (called from a Script, tested), or a separate place. It must NOT suggest writing StreamingIntegrityMode/StreamingMinRadius/StreamingTargetRadius from a script (NotScriptable). FAILS if it writes workspace.StreamingEnabled = ... as working code.

evals.prompt: Write a server Script that damages players who touch a lava part and prints each lava MeshPart's CollisionFidelity
evals.notes: Over-correction guard for the PluginOrOpenCloud lesson. Humanoid.Health needs the AvatarBehavior capability, which an ordinary Script DOES hold, and reading CollisionFidelity is allowed: both work from a plain server Script in Studio 0.742 (tested 2026-10-11). Correct answer writes the Touched handler with humanoid health changes and reads CollisionFidelity, without claiming either needs a plugin. FAILS if it says the Script cannot do either.

evals.prompt: My ProcessReceipt handler returns false when the player's data isn't loaded yet, but players still get charged and receive nothing. Here's my code: local success = pcall(handler, player) if success then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted end
evals.notes: pcall's first value is only 'did not error'; the handler's false is ignored, so PurchaseGranted is returned for a grant that did not happen. Correct answer checks `ok and granted == true`, returns NotProcessedYet otherwise (the purchase is retried on rejoin, never dropped by that answer), and makes the handler idempotent on PurchaseId (record and grant in one UpdateAsync). Studio 0.742: the corrected pattern passed all five receipt cases. FAILS if it keeps `if success then`.

evals.prompt: I renamed the saved field Coins to coins and changed inventory from a list to counts. Easiest is to just use a new DataStore name PlayerData_v2, right?
evals.notes: A new DataStore name is an empty store: every player loses progress. Correct answer keeps the name, adds a version field, migrates on load step by step (data with no version = v1), refuses saves newer than the server knows, and never falls back to defaults on a failed read. FAILS if it recommends the new store name without a migration of the old data.

evals.prompt: Make pressing B (and Y on gamepad) open my shop GUI using the new Input Action System
evals.notes: Client-only: an InputAction (Type Bool) under an InputContext with one InputBinding per device (KeyCode B, KeyCode ButtonY, touch via UIButton), and a LocalScript listening to Pressed that toggles the ScreenGui. Verified in Studio 0.742 with a real key press. FAILS if it routes the toggle through a RemoteEvent, uses non-existent members (Activated, InputType, Enum.InputActionType.Button), or tries to set PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem from a script.

evals.prompt: Why does Roblox not catch type errors in this script? The first line is: --!strict -- enforce types
evals.notes: A directive line with anything after it is ignored: luau-analyze 0.742 reports 'Comment directive with the type checking mode has extra symbols at the end of the line' and checks the file in the default nonstrict mode. Correct answer: put only `--!strict` on that line and move the comment down. FAILS if it blames something else.

evals.prompt: Give each new player default data: local DEFAULT = table.freeze({Coins = 0, Inventory = {}}) then sessionData[player] = table.clone(DEFAULT)
evals.notes: table.clone is shallow: every clone shares DEFAULT.Inventory, so an item given to one player appears for all (reproduced in Studio 0.742). Correct answer builds a fresh table per player (a defaultData() function) or deep-copies. FAILS if it accepts the shallow clone.

evals.prompt: Run my pathfinding in parallel: RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel(function() ... end) in a Script in ServerScriptService
evals.notes: ConnectParallel and task.desynchronize only work in a Script that is a descendant of an Actor; in ServerScriptService it errors 'Scripts that connect in parallel must be rooted under an Actor' (Studio 0.742). Correct answer moves the Script under an Actor (one per independent unit) and keeps DataModel writes after task.synchronize(). FAILS if it presents the snippet as working where it is.
